## Thermodynamics as the equation of state of snapy (thermodynamics card) {#sec-ch14-thermo}

### Summary

snapy's moist equations of state do not carry their own thermodynamic data. They hold a kintera `ThermoY` module
built from the same card and take every molar mass and the gas constant from it. The `moist-mixture` type converts
between density, internal energy, pressure and temperature by calling kintera. The `ideal-moist` type, which five of
the six moist example decks of snapy use, writes the same conversions in closed form. This section derives both
from the state snapy holds and shows that each conversion inverts the other with one gas constant and one set of
molar masses.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The units and variables at the equation-of-state interface, @eq-ch14-thermo-split to
@eq-ch14-thermo-mole, and the `ideal-moist` closed form, @eq-ch14-thermo-ideal-moist.

**Data.** Density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], mass fractions [-], internal energy [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$], $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa].

**Placement.** Every primitive/conserved conversion in snapy's moist equations of state.

**Activation.** The thermodynamics card of the snapy input; always on for a moist equation of state.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact inverses for a linear card; `ideal-moist` agrees with kintera only for a linear card.

**Evidence.** `check_ch14_coupling.py` lines (a) to (j); see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho$, total density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$]; $\rho_0$, dry density; $\rho_i$, partial density of
species $i \ge 1$; $y_i = \rho_i/\rho$, mass fraction; $\mu_i$, molar mass [$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $c_i$,
concentration [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $E$, total energy per volume; $e_k$, kinetic energy per volume; $U$, internal
energy per volume [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$]; $c_{v,i}$, isochoric heat capacity per mole in units of $\mathcal R$ [-] (the card's `cv_R`[^rg-5d1f6c2e39d3]); $u_i^0$,
energy offset of species $i$ at $T = 0$ per mole in units of $\mathcal R$ [K]; $\hat c_{v,i} = \mathcal R c_{v,i}/\mu_i$
[$\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$] and $\hat u_i^0 = \mathcal R u_i^0/\mu_i$ [$\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$], the same per unit mass;
$R_d = \mathcal R/\mu_0$, the dry gas constant; $\gamma_d$, the dry ratio of heat capacities.

### Derivation

**What snapy holds.** snapy's conserved state keeps the dry density $\rho_0$ in row `IDN`, the partial densities
$\rho_i$ of the vapours and clouds in the rows from `ICY` on, and the total energy $E$ in row `IPR`
([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:93-121`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L93-L121)). Its primitive state keeps the total density and the mass fractions (`div_out`,
[`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:131-138`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L131-L138)), and the internal energy is $U = E - e_k$
(`ke`, [`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:146-147`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L146-L147)).

**Step 1: partial densities.** kintera's state "V" is the vector of partial densities with the dry gas first. From
$\rho$ and the mass fractions of the non-dry species,

$$
\rho_0 = \rho \Big(1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} y_i\Big), \qquad \rho_i = \rho\, y_i \quad [\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}] ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-thermo-split}

which is `DY->V` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol >}}); `V->Y` divides by
$\sum_i \rho_i$ again.

**Step 2: concentrations.** Every function of `ThermoY` turns V into concentrations by
$c_i = \rho_i/\mu_i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$], with $1/\mu_i$ the buffer `inv_mu` made from the card's molar masses
in `reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}). snapy takes every molar mass from the same
`inv_mu` ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:24`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L24), `inv_mu` at [`:34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L34)) and the gas constant from kintera's
`constants::Rgas` ({{< code src/constants.h >}}; [`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:38`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L38)). There is one $\mathcal R$ and
one set of molar masses on both sides by construction.

**Step 3: internal energy.** `reset` moves each energy offset of the card to $T = 0$,
$u_i^0 = u_{i,\mathrm{card}} - c_{v,i} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$, once, on the options object
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}). The energy per volume is the sum of the molar energies
times the concentrations,

$$
U = \sum_i c_i\, \mathcal R \big(u_i^0 + c_{v,i} T\big) \quad [\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}] ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-thermo-energy}

the linear model of `eval_intEng_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_intEng_R >}}), returned by `VT->U`
([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:166`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L166)). It is linear in $T$, so `VU->T`, a Newton iteration on
@eq-ch14-thermo-energy ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}}), is exact after one step.

**Step 4: pressure.** Only the gases carry pressure. With compressibility $z = 1$,

$$
p = \mathcal R T \sum_{\mathrm{gas}} c_i = \mathcal R T \sum_{\mathrm{gas}} \frac{\rho_i}{\mu_i} \quad [\mathrm{Pa}] ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-thermo-pressure}

which is `VT->P` ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:151`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L151)). It inverts to $T = p/(\mathcal R \sum_{\mathrm{gas}} c_i)$, which
is the starting value of `PV->T` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_pres_to_temp >}};
[`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:290`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L290)).

**Step 5: mole fractions.** The drivers of @sec-ch14-kinetics call `Y->X`. Dividing each mass fraction by its molar
mass and normalising, with the dry gas and the clouds included,

$$
x_i = \frac{y_i/\mu_i}{\sum_j y_j/\mu_j} ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-thermo-mole}

which is the closed form of `Y->X` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac >}}) after
division by $1/\mu_0$.

**Step 6: the `ideal-moist` closed form.** `IdealMoist` does not call `VT->U`. It works per unit mass and reads
$\hat u_i^0 = \mathcal R u_i^0/\mu_i$ from the options object after `ThermoYImpl::create`
([`snapy ideal_moist.cpp:20`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L20), `u0` at [`:48-51`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L48-L51)). `create` runs `reset`, which shifts the
offsets in place and sets `offset_zero`, and the options object is shared, so snapy reads the shifted values. It
uses
$f_\sigma = 1 + \sum_i y_i (\hat c_{v,i}/\hat c_{v,d} - 1)$ and
$f_\epsilon = 1 + \sum_{\mathrm{vap}} y_i (\mu_d/\mu_i - 1) - \sum_{\mathrm{cloud}} y_i$
(`f_eps`, `f_sig`, [`snapy ideal_moist.cpp:330-357`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L330-L357)). By @eq-ch14-thermo-pressure, $p = \rho R_d T f_\epsilon$. Since
$\hat c_{v,d} = R_d/(\gamma_d - 1)$, $p/(\gamma_d - 1) = \rho\, \hat c_{v,d} T f_\epsilon$, and

$$
U = \frac{p\, f_\sigma}{f_\epsilon (\gamma_d - 1)} + \rho \sum_i y_i \hat u_i^0 = T \sum_i \rho_i \hat c_{v,i} + \sum_i \rho_i \hat u_i^0 ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-thermo-ideal-moist}

clouds included, which is @eq-ch14-thermo-energy because $\rho_i \hat c_{v,i} = c_i \mathcal R c_{v,i}$ and
$\rho_i \hat u_i^0 = c_i \mathcal R u_i^0$. That is the internal energy of
`f_sig` in [`snapy ideal_moist.cpp:225-231`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L225-L231), and $T = p/(\rho R_d f_\epsilon)$ is its temperature
(`f_eps`, [`snapy ideal_moist.cpp:241`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L241)). The identity needs $z = 1$ and no NASA-9, H$_2$ or extra energy terms
(Limits).

The check builds the state as snapy builds it, on the Jupiter deck, in six cells from 140 K to 300 K and 0.5 to
6 bar, supersaturated.[^ch14-check-thermo]

- "(a) DY->V (snapy moist_mixture.cpp:149) against rho*(1-sum y), rho*y: max rel err 1.97e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"
- "(b) V->Y after DY->V returns the mass fractions: max rel err 3.62e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"
- "(c) VT->U [J/m^3] against sum c_i R (u0_i - cv_i Tref + cv_i T), c = rho_i/mu_i: max rel err 2.33e-16 (tol 1e-12) PASS"
- "(d) VU->T(VT->U(T)) round trip (moist_mixture.cpp:150): max rel err 2.22e-16 (tol 1e-10) PASS"
- "(e) VT->P against R T sum_gas rho_i/mu_i (moist_mixture.cpp:151): max rel err 4.44e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"
- "(f) PV->T (moist_mixture.cpp:290) inverts VT->P: max rel err 4.44e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"
- "(g) Y->X (run_hydro.cpp:179) against x_i = (y_i/mu_i)/sum_j(y_j/mu_j), dry included: max rel err 3.47e-18 (tol 1e-15) PASS"
- "(h) IdealMoist W->I formula against kintera VT->U at the same state: max rel err 4.95e-16 (tol 1e-12) PASS"
- "(i) IdealMoist W->T = p/(rho Rd f_eps) against the state temperature: max rel err 3.33e-16 (tol 1e-13) PASS"
- "(j) the options object snapy reads after ThermoYImpl::create holds the T=0 offsets (uref - cref Tref): True PASS"

No published derivation is quoted. The steps are the ideal-gas law and the linear energy model of @sec-ch03, matched
to the code at the two pins.

### Numerical method

No numerical method of its own. The `moist-mixture` type converts with `compute` and the string keys above
([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:149-151`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L149-L151)) and calls the free functions `eval_cv_R`, `eval_cp_R`, `eval_czh` and
`eval_czh_ddC` for heat capacities and compressibility terms ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:245-262`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L245-L262)). Before it
reads species names and molar masses, the equation of state calls `populate_thermo`
({{< code src/species.cpp populate_thermo >}}, [`snapy equation_of_state.cpp:128`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L128)), so that it uses the copy of the species
table held by its own options rather than kintera's process-wide table. A card without a `reference-state`[^rg-7efe2bd33a7d] block
gives no thermodynamics options ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}), and snapy
then runs a dry equation of state. Output diagnostics call `relative_humidity`
({{< code src/thermo/relative_humidity.cpp relative_humidity >}}, [`snapy load_diag_output_data.cpp:113`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/output/load_diag_output_data.cpp#L113)).

The figure of the call graph is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Limits

- `_prim2speciesEng` passes the partial densities, in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, where `eval_intEng_R` expects
  concentrations ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:185`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L185)); the sibling `species_enthalpy` passes
  `ivol * inv_mu`. `eval_intEng_R` uses that argument only through the user extra-energy functions, and none is
  registered at the pin, so no result changes. This is suspect S14-2, latent.[^ch14-s14-2]
- @eq-ch14-thermo-ideal-moist holds for a linear card only. With NASA-9 data or the H$_2$ heat capacity on, kintera's
  energy and `IdealMoist`'s closed form differ. This is suspect S14-3, latent; the in-tree Jupiter deck is linear.
- Three snapy example decks give the NH$_3$ vapour the composition of water, so its molar mass differs from that of
  its condensates. That is an input defect of those decks, handled on the snapy side; kintera's readers accept it
  because they do not check element balance (latent K29 row of the issue below).[^ch14-k29]
